Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
This proposed revision has been 
filed under Section 25 of the Provincial 
Small Cause Courts Act, 1887, against 
the judgment and decree dated 
03.08.2019 along with an application 
for condonation of delay.
Heard Mr. P.C. Maulekhi, learned 
counsel for the applicant.
The learned counsel for the 
applicant submitted that the matter is 
very urgent and requested to consider 
the Stay application. He further 
submitted that the lower court record 
should be summoned. 
Having heard the learned counsel, 
it seems appropriate to issue notice to 
the respondent on the delay 
condonation application before passing 
any order on the Stay application or 
before passing any order to summon 
the original record. 
Issue notice to the respondent. 
Steps to be taken forthwith. 
List this case on 11.05.2022.

applicant today itself on payment of 
usual charges.

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma
orders.text:
SL. 
No Date
Office Notes, reports, 
orders or proceedings or 
directions and Registrar’s 
order with Signatures
COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CLR No. 22 of 2022
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. P.C. Maulekhi, Advocate for the 
revisionist.
Mr. Sanjeev Kumar Sah, Advocate for the 
respondent.
The petitioner before this Court is a defendant. 
in an SCC suit proceedings which was held by way of 
SCC Case No. 19 of 2017, Suresh Chandra Vs. 
Deewan Singh Bohra. The suit was decreed by the 
judgement of 03.08.2019. Being aggrieved against the 
aforesaid judgment passed by the Judge, Small 
Causes Court, whereby a decree of an eviction and 
recovery of arrears of rent was rendered against the 
present revisionist. This revision was preferred on 
03.08.2019 accompanied with a delay condonation 
application preferred by the revisionist where the 
reason for delay has been more appropriately 
described in paragraph 5, 6 and 11 of the affidavit 
filed in support of delay condonation application,
which is extracted hereunder:-
“5. That after receiving the certified copy of the order dated 
03.08.2019 as well as the decree dated 13.08.2019 the counsel of the 
trial court Shri. Manoj Bhatt advised the deponent /revisionist to 
challenge the impugned judgement and decree by way of filing 
revision before the Hon'ble High Court therefore the wife of the 
deponent contacted Shri. Dushyant Mainali Advocate High Court at 
his office at Haldwani and instructed him to file a revision against 
the impugned judgement dated 03.082019 and decree dated  13.08.2019 before the Hon’ble High Court and paid all the before 
the Hon'ble High Court and paid all the necessary expenses and the 
requisite fee of the counsel after handing over the entire record of 
the case to Shri. Dushyant Mainali, Advocate High Court and the 
wife of the deponent also informed him that the deponent is 
suffering from asthma and due to his old age he could not come to 
Nainital regularly and Shri. Dushyant Mainali Advocate made a 
promise to the wife of the deponent that he will file the aforesaid
revision against the impugned judgement and decree dated 
03.08.2019 and 13.08.2019 as such after the assurance so given by 
Shri Dushyant Mainali to the wife of deponent, the deponent as
communicated to him the same by her wife was under the hope that 
his advocate will file the aforesaid revision within time and will take 
necessary stay order from the High Court.
6. That several times the deponent made an enquiry telephonically 
from his advocate above named i.e. Shri Dushyant Mainali about the 
matter but he assured and convinced the deponent that the aforesaid
revision has been filed before the Hon'ble High Court but the said 
revision could not be listed for final hearing due to COVID -19 and 
the stay order so obtained in the revision so filed by the advocate of 
the deponent Shri. Dushyant Mainali against the impugned 
judgement and decree dated 03.08.2019 has been produced before 
the Judge S.C.C. in S.C.C Case No. 19 of 2019 "Suresh Chandra V/s 
Diwan Singh Bora."
11. That there was no communication about the progress of the case 
from the side of the advocate of the deponent i.e. Shri Dushyant 
Mainali and when on 29.03.2022 the facts came to the knowledge of 
the deponent about the issuance of Parwana for handing over the 
possession then on 30.03.2022 the deponent came to Nainital and 
enquired the matter regarding filing of the aforesaid Civil Revision 
wherein he came to know that no aforesaid Civil Revision has been 
filed by Shri. Dushyant Mainali against the impugned judgement and 
decree before the Hon'ble High Court till today. The deponent is an 
old and illiterate person and is suffering from asthma thereby when 
it came to the knowledge of the deponent that no revision has been 
filed by the advocate engaged by him Shri Dushyant Mainali since
2019 therefore the deponent was shocked by the conduct of his 
advocate toward the deponent.”
Though, at this stage, it would be too
premature to record any statement with regards to the 
conduct of the counsel, whose name has been  specifically referred to in the affidavit filed in support 
of the delay condonation application, because that 
would be exclusively a subject matter to be decided 
by the registering body of the counsel concerned i.e. 
the Uttarakhand Bar Council, because no professional 
registered with the Bar Council could be permitted to 
take liberty and play foul with a litigant by giving a 
wrongful understanding of taking the brief! informing 
the client that he has filed the case! thereafter 
informing him that he has got a stay order in his 
favour! thereafter making a statement that the stay 
order has been filed before the executing court! All 
these statements are per se apparently false because 
there is no prior pending revision, than the one at 
hand which has been instituted and there is no reason 
to disbelief the grounds taken by the revisionist in the 
delay condonation application of the Assurances
extended by the counsel Mr Dushyant Manali. This 
false assurance extended by counsel for the 
revisionist as per the opinion of this court is of the 
view is tentatively and apparently true would amount 
to be a professional misconduct for which this Court 
is taking a suo moto cognizance and referring the 
matter to the bar council to draw an appropriate 
proceedings disciplinary against the counsel 
concerned for wrongful extension of information to 
the litigant due to which the revision had preferred 
the revision at a belated stage, when the revisionist 
faced the order passed by the executing court in 
pursuance to the impugned decree which has been put 
to challenge in the present revision. The Bar Council is directed to proceed strictly in 
accordance with the procedures governing with the 
disciplinary proceedings of the bar council as well as 
under the provisions of the Advocates act. Having 
apparently considered the reasons which has been 
given in the delay condonation application, logically 
this Court is of the view that any litigant 
blindfoldedly relies upon the statement given by the 
counsel and he acts upon that and in all the 
circumstances, it is not necessary that the said 
communication made by the counsel to the client has 
had to be in writing. In that eventuality, prima facie
and so far as the revisionist is concerned individually, 
he cannot be held responsible for delayed filing of a 
revision when the revisionist counsel Mr. Dushyant 
Mainali has duped him by making a false statement,
which was bonafidely believed by the revisionist. In 
that eventuality, this court directs the Registrar 
General of this Court to refer the matter to the Bar 
Council of Uttarakhand to draw and appropriate 
disciplinary proceedings against the professional
misconduct on part of Mr. Dushyant Mainali and to 
conduct and conclude the proceedings against him 
within a period of six months from today and report 
back to this Court of decision taken.
Having considered the reasons given in the 
delay condonation application and also after 
considering the objection raised by the respondent to 
the delay condonation application, particularly in the 
context of the reply given to paragraph 5, 6, 11 and  14, the contents of which, have not been specifically 
denied and quite logically too, because the grounds
taken in paragraph 5, 6, 11 and 14 may not be within 
the knowledge of the deponent who has objected the 
delay condonation application, but, still the petitioner 
cannot be held to be exclusively responsible for 
belated filing of the revision. In that eventuality, the 
delay which has chanced in preferring the revision 
with the delay of 226 days, would hereby stand 
condoned.
The revision is directed to be listed next week 
for hearing at admission stage immediately after 
fresh.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 20.06.2022
Ujjwal

Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. P.C. Maulekhi, Advocate, for the 
revisionist.
Mr. Sanjeev Kumar Sah, Advocate, 
for the respondent.
Admit.
No notice is required to be sent to 
the respondent, as he is already represented 
by Mr. Sanjeev Kumar Sah, Advocate. 
Since the decree in question,
happens to be a decree, which has been 
rendered in a proceeding under Section 15 
of the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 
1887, as rendered in SCC Case No. 19 of 
2017, Suresh Chandra Vs. Diwan Singh Bora, 
which takes the shape of regular proceeding 
which has been put to challenge in the 
present SCC Revision under Section 25 of 
the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act. 
There would be an interim order to 
the effect, that the execution of the 
impugned decree dated 03.08.2019, would 
be kept in abeyance, subject to the 
following conditions:-
(i) The revisionist deposits the entire 
decreetal amount, as settled by the 
impugned decree, before the Judge, Small 
Causes, Haldwani, Nainital, within a period 
of six weeks from today.
(ii) The interim order would be 
effective subject to the condition, that  revisionist continues to remit the monthly 
rent, as determined by the impugned order 
i.e. Rs. 2250/- per month, by paying the 
same to the respondent by 10th of each 
month.
Non-compliance of any of the above 
conditions would automatically result into 
vacating the interim order granted by this 
Court vide its today’s order and the decree 
would be put to execution by the 
respondent.
Let a certified copy of this order be 
supplied to the parties within 48 hours’ 
time, on payment of usual charges.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 30.06.2022
